lines.text: Here's what our simulator says. Every run starts two point eight meters back, a bit to the side, already moving.
A success means the robot says it's done, and it's truly within two centimeters and one degree.
Driving to the map: fifty seven, thirty one, fifteen percent, as the simulated world gets messier.
Tracking the tag in the wheel world, without calibration: one hundred, seventy two, forty six.
Add per-camera calibration and the retuned drive loop: one hundred, ninety nine, ninety eight.
On the hard world: no calibration, sixty six. Teaching the goal spot instead, sixty four. Fixing each camera, one hundred.
One center camera: seventy three to seventy eight percent. Two corner cameras: one hundred.
Frame rate, pixel noise, and handoff speed barely mattered. These are simulator numbers with guessed errors. Robot tests will replace them.
